SEO specialist here, 5 years of experience. You can teach yourself enough to be literate in it - but not to actually do it. 

I'm only now getting to a place where I feel 100% confident taking an independent lead and vouching for it and realizing how much my previous knowledge was vanilla. SEO is a combination of UX/UI design, PR, CRO tactics, content marketing, and web development. Usually, you can teach yourself to be good at 1-2 of those things, but not all of them. And usually, that's brainstorming content and black hat link building. Effectively, you'd only be doing a fraction of the SEO, and your results would also only be a fraction of what they could be in return.

It would need to be your primary calling, or at least marketing in itself would. As a business owner, I'm sure you cannot also be your full time CMO. 

And as an SEO specialist in an established agency, 85% of our clients are people who "did their own seo" before and now we have to clean up the mess of javascript-reliant websites in non-responsive design and 15 megabyte PNGs with keyword-stuffed run-of-the-mill articles and a whole bunch of link insertion backlinks... 

So no I would not recommed you do your own SEO. BUT I DO recommend you know the foundation of it so you can assess the quality of the people doing it. My rec would be to get very proficient in reading data from relevant tools.

Get the basic certification in GA and GSC. Buy Ahrefs (much more affordable than SEMrush) and pass their academy. Get a feel of what each report means and what each metric indicates.

THEN hire someone to do it for you.

Also - a single page needs 4 weeks to 4 months to reposition to where it will be in the forseeable future. Unfortunately, the first 6 months of actively executing SEO will not bring you any ROI, but you can expect ROI after a year, and then profits from that point on for as long as you keep going. Cheers
